content.title: About
content.content: Wheat bran is the outer layer of the wheat grain obtained during milling. It is rich in dietary fiber, B‑vitamins, and minerals. In Muffin, wheat bran, the bran is used as the main ingredient, giving the baked good a nutty aroma and boosting its nutritional value.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Bran contains over 10 % protein and up to 30 % dietary fiber.
The fiber in bran helps regulate bowel movements and supports gut health.
Wheat bran is frequently used in diet and sports nutrition to increase satiety.
Bran contains phytoestrogens that may have a positive effect on hormonal balance.
It can be used as a natural thickener in sauces and soups.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Fiber improves digestion, promotes regular stools, and supports a healthy intestinal microbiome.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: B1, B2, B3 and folate are involved in energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: Magnesium, iron and zinc in bran are important for muscle function, blood formation and immunity.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Bran raises blood sugar slowly, which is beneficial for weight control and diabetes management.

items.title: Promotes satiety
items.content: The high fiber content slows stomach emptying, helping you feel full longer.

items.title: Wheat allergy
items.content: People with wheat allergy or celiac disease may react to bran.

items.title: Excessive fiber intake
items.content: Too much bran can cause bloating, gas and abdominal discomfort.

items.title: Medication interactions
items.content: Fiber may reduce the absorption of certain drugs; take medicines separately from bran.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Wheat bran can be mixed into muffin, bread, pancake batters, added to yogurt, oatmeal, smoothies, or sprinkled over salads. It is also used as a coating for fish and meat.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store bran in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For long‑term storage keep it in the refrigerator to prevent fat oxidation.
